interface.title: Assay Analyzer
interface.field: Food and plant biochemistry: phytochemical, antioxidant, anti-nutrient, oil-quality and mineral (AAS) assays
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis and quality control of bench measurements, then reporting
interface.what_it_is_for: Turns bench readings (absorbance, titre, mass, AAS) or already-calculated results into assay results with standard-curve, replicate-CV, out-of-range and non-detect checks, ANOVA/Tukey letters, reference or target comparisons and an Excel report.

data.note: Started on the built-in 'Supplied results tables' example: 76 calculated observations transcribed from cotton-result-only.pdf. Switched to the built-in 'Synthetic bench readings' example. Then turned example data off and uploaded tpc.csv, dpph.csv, minerals.csv and provided_results.csv. I edited one tpc absorbance by hand in the entry grid to trigger the out-of-range flag. The app only answered on http://localhost:8501; 127.0.0.1 stayed on a blank 'Running' page (first screenshots of the run, not kept).

tree.specific: Compute phytochemical, antioxidant, anti-nutrient, oil-quality and mineral assay results (e.g. for cottonseed extracts) with QC flags, Tukey letters and an Excel report

features.name: Standard curve with range and fit checks
features.general: Fit a linear calibration from standards, read samples off it, report the equation and R², and warn when the fit is poor or a sample lies beyond the highest standard
features.specific: Absorbance vs standard concentration plot with standards (blue) and samples read off the curve (orange), annotated 'A = 0.0021035·C + 0.0005 (R² = 0.9997)'; 'What should I check?' lists 'absorbance above the highest standard… Dilute the extract and re-read' or 'calibration R² is 0.9915 (below 0.995)'
steps: load standards and sample readings
view the fitted curve with equation and R²
edit a sample reading beyond the top standard
re-analyse and read the extrapolation or poor-fit warning
serves_tasks: Fit the calibration line and check its goodness of fit
Find samples that read outside the calibrated range so they can be diluted and re-measured

features.name: Replicate variability check with a culprit reading
features.general: Compute each replicate set's coefficient of variation, flag sets above a chosen limit, and name the replicate furthest from the mean
features.specific: 'replicate CV is 26.3% (limit 10%). Replicate 1 deviates most from the mean; check it against your notebook'; the limit is set in Settings > Flag repeats that vary by more than (%)
steps: set the CV limit in Settings
open What should I check? on an assay
read which set and which replicate are flagged
raise or lower the limit and see the flag list change
serves_tasks: Find replicate sets with too much spread and the reading most likely at fault
Name the study and choose how replicate spread, variability limit and significance level are set

features.name: Grouped comparison with compact letter display
features.general: Run ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc tests across samples in one assay and show the groups as letters on a mean ± error bar chart and in the table
features.specific: Horizontal bars of mean ± SEM/SD labelled '69.6 a', '4.05 b'; caption 'Bars sharing a letter are not significantly different (Tukey HSD, α = 0.05)'; α and SEM/SD are chosen in Settings
steps: load replicate results for several samples
choose α (0.01/0.05/0.1) and SEM or SD
read the letters on the bar chart and in the result table
serves_tasks: Test whether samples within one assay differ and show the groups with letters

features.name: Dose-response fit with IC50
features.general: Fit sigmoid curves of response against log concentration for each sample, mark the 50% line, and compare the fitted IC50 values with error bars and letters
features.specific: 'DPPH radical scavenging' plot of inhibition (%) vs concentration (µg/mL, log scale) with a 50% dashed line and an IC50 in the legend; a 'DPPH IC50' bar chart with Tukey letters ('a' = lowest IC50); the IC50 method (logistic) is shown under Advanced: dose-response fitting (only the logistic method was used)
steps: load a concentration series per sample
check the IC50 method under Advanced: dose-response fitting
view the fitted curves
compare IC50 bars and letters
serves_tasks: Fit dose-response curves and estimate the half-maximal concentration

features.name: Reference / target-range flag table
features.general: Compare each sample's mean with a measured reference sample or a numeric target range and colour-code the outcome with a suggested next step
features.specific: Settings > Compare results with (Off / Reference sample / Target range), Measurement to check (Result / IC50), lower and upper values, unit and source; the 'Reference and target checks' table shows Within target / Above target / Below reference / Needs review / No matching reference. Configured in Settings only in target-range mode; reference flags were seen via the example's supplied ascorbic acid reference button
steps: pick an assay to configure
choose reference sample or target range
set the measurement, limits and unit
save
read the colour-coded flags on the assay page and Overview
serves_tasks: Flag each sample against a measured reference sample
Flag each sample against a target range
Choose what each assay's results are compared against

features.name: Readings intake: upload or editable grid
features.general: Show the columns an assay expects, then accept the measurements as an uploaded CSV/XLSX or in an editable grid, re-analyse on demand and clear
features.specific: '1 · Values you need' column guide, Download a data-entry template, the 'Upload a file' / 'Enter readings here' radio, a data-editor grid with + row, 'Analyze these readings' and 'Clear these readings'
steps: read the column guide
choose Upload a file or Enter readings here
upload a CSV or edit grid cells
press Analyze these readings
clear to start over
serves_tasks: Upload a file of raw bench readings for one assay
Type or edit readings in an on-screen grid and re-analyse

features.name: Calculated-results import with repeat pooling
features.general: Import a long table of already-calculated values, choose whether rows sharing a group label are pooled as repeats, and break the results down per measurement with the source rows kept
features.specific: Calculated results page: upload provided_results.csv, tick 'group_id labels confirmed repeats' (uploads) or 'Combine the confirmed repeat measurements' (example data), read the summary metrics and table, open per-assay expanders with a summary (n, mean, sd, sem, cv_pct, letters) and 'Source observations'
steps: upload the calculated table
tick or untick repeat pooling
read the summary table
open an assay expander to see statistics and source rows
serves_tasks: Import a table of results that were already calculated
Choose whether confirmed repeat measurements are pooled before statistics

features.name: Small-multiple panel chart with non-detects
features.general: Draw one small bar panel per analyte, each on its own scale, and label values below the detection limit as ND instead of plotting zero
features.specific: 'Mineral elements (mg/kg, AAS)' grid of Ca, K, Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu, Pb, Cd panels with error bars and ND labels (screens/046.webp); after minerals.csv was uploaded (screens/060.webp) only the result table's ND cells showed and the Charts area was empty
steps: load multi-element readings in long format
view the per-element panels
read the ND markers and the matching ND cells in the result table
